newsitem.title: UK: Romania seeks careful fall in rates, stable forex.
newsitem.headline: Romania seeks careful fall in rates, stable forex.

text.p: National Bank of Romania's head Mugur Isarescu said the bank would like to engineer a careful reduction in interest rates and still maintain confidence in the leu.
Isarescu told a group of investors late on Thursday that Romania was walking a fine line in its monetary policy.
"The very difficult target is to maintain a tough monetary policy but accept that the market will induce a reduction of rates with a slide in inflation," he said.
"We would also like to consolidate the market exchange rate and the credibility of the foreign exchange policy."
Romania tightened monetary policy earlier this year to stifle soaring inflation after liberalising the foreign exchange market and fuel, energy and food prices.
Inflation slowed to a monthly rate of 6.9 percent last month after a record 30.7 percent in March, and is expected to fall to two to three percent by year-end.

With the leu stabilising near 7,100 to the dollar after February's 9,000 all-time low, the market was flooded with dollar inflows allowing the central bank (BNR) to soak up the excess and build reserves.
But BNR dollar purchases fuelled leu liquidity and with few tools to mop up excess funds, money market rates fell rapidly to around 60 percent from 190 in April.
Isarescu said there was a need to diversify BNR liquidity management instruments but he expressed doubts that there was a real excess of leu on the local market.
"I'm sure this is a relative excess of liquidity," he said, noting that soon there would be a need for leu funds with economic activity resuming and expectations of a bumper wheat crop this summer.
"Unfortunately our T-bill portfolio is limited." he said adding that he preferred government securities to manage the liquidity rather than a proposed issue of BNR certificates of deposits.

Attractive yields and rising foreign interest in Romanian equities has kept the local market dollar-heavy over the past months. The BNR meanwhile has been buying dollars to keep the leu competitive for exporters.

With a new law on portfolio investments due for approval soon, foreign inflows are expected to grow further and the upward trend in the BNR's reserves, currently at $1.6 billion, is likely to continue, Isarescu said.

"Rising reserves and lower inflation would also allow us to give up the $500 limit on the annual hard currency buying by (Romanian) individuals. This will also boost confidence," Isarescu said. -- London Newsroom 171 542 6414
